overall_feedback: This is a carefully executed antidot experiment that adds a local air-bridge gate to a gate-defined BLG antidot, and it reports gate-voltage periods at nu = -5/2, -1/2 and 3/2 whose ratio to an integer reference is about 0.25. The ADG calibration against nu = -1 and -4/3, the conservative treatment of the -5/2 uncertainty, the histogram cross-check at nu = 2/3 and the explicit caveat that a gate period measures the change in localized charge, not the tunnelling charge, are all strengths. The e/4 conclusion rests almost entirely on Delta V/Delta V1, which is reasonably robust. The supporting and interpretive material is weaker. Using the quoted Delta B1 = 40.3 mT, the minimal-regime magnetic periods give p of about 6.8, 3.1 and 7.6 rather than the stated 10, 2 and 6, and they do not order as expected. The electron-side states (2/3, 3/2) are normalized to a hole-side reference that was never checked on the electron side. Several statements about the doubled regime contradict each other: nu = 3/2 is said to have a double/minimal B ratio close to 2 and also p of about 1, and the -1/2 doubled period is extracted from less than one period in the scan window. The 'factor of ten' area argument is overstated. The claimed absence of doubling at odd-denominator states is not shown at comparable coupling (nu = -1/3 was never taken to positive side-gate voltage). The bunching scenario and the nu_LL interferometry phenomenology predict identical gate ratios for every state studied, so the gate data cannot discriminate between them. The temperature scales quoted in the main text and the supplement disagree, and the electron temperature is inferred, not measured. The capacitive argument in Supp. E does not support the conclusion it is used for. None of this overturns the main e/4 observation, but the crossover discussion needs tightening and several numbers need reconciling.

comments.title: Contradictory statements about the nu = 3/2 magnetic-field period in the doubled regime
comments.quote: ν = 3/2 approaches close to 2 within uncertainty, while
comments.explanation: At first I read this as a modest statement that the doubled-regime B period at 3/2 is roughly twice the minimal one, as bunching would predict. The Discussion then says that in the doubled regime 'at ν = 3/2 the magnetic-field periodicity corresponds to p ≈ 1', and later that 3/2 falls 'close to ∆B1/∆B = 1, as expected in the AB regime'. The minimal-regime 3/2 period is ∆B = 5.3 ± 1.4 mT, i.e. ∆B1/∆B ≈ 40.3/5.3 ≈ 7.6 (quoted as p ≈ 6). If the doubled regime has p ≈ 1, then ∆B_double/∆B_minimal ≈ 6 to 7.6, not about 2. Simple bunching would predict p/2 = 3, not 1. Both statements cannot be true for the same datasets unless the minimal-regime 3/2 data in Fig. 3 differ from Fig. 2, which the text does not say. This matters because 3/2 is used in one paragraph as near-consistent with bunching and in another as evidence for an AB-like regime.
comments.suggested_fix: Quote the numerical values of ∆B_minimal, ∆B_double and their ratio for ν = 3/2 in the text. If the doubled regime gives p ≈ 1, replace 'approaches close to 2 within uncertainty' with the actual ratio (about 6) and state that 3/2 is inconsistent with the simple bunching prediction p/2 = 3.

comments.title: nu = -2/3 is not a measured state; and at nu = 2/3 bunching and AB predictions coincide
comments.quote: In our case the magnetic field periodicities at ν = −2/3
comments.explanation: ν = −2/3 appears nowhere else among the measured states, so this is presumably ν = 2/3. That alone is a slip. The more substantive problem is that at ν = 2/3 the bunching picture predicts p/2 = 2/2 = 1 for the doubled regime, which is the same as the AB-limit value ∆B1/∆B = 1. The bunching paragraph counts ν = 2/3 as consistent with doubling of the B period, and this paragraph counts it as consistent with the AB regime. Because the two predictions coincide, ν = 2/3 cannot discriminate between the scenarios, and presenting it as support for each in turn overstates the evidence. The only state whose B data discriminate in favour of bunching is ν = −5/2, where bunching gives p/2 = 5 and AB gives 1.
comments.suggested_fix: Replace ν = −2/3 with ν = 2/3 and add: 'At ν = 2/3 the bunching prediction p/2 = 1 coincides with the AB value ∆B1/∆B = 1, so this state does not distinguish the two scenarios; the distinction rests on ν = −5/2.'

comments.title: Measured minimal-regime B periods do not reproduce the stated p = 10, 2, 6
comments.quote: respond approximately to p = 10, 2, and 6 quasiparticles
comments.explanation: The expected values follow the CD relation p = |ν|e/q (which gives 4 at −4/3, 2 at 2/3, 1 at −1/3, and 10, 2, 6 for e/4 at −5/2, −1/2, 3/2). That relation is never written in the main text, and the citations [2, 33] (a qubit proposal and Read-Rezayi zero modes) do not derive antidot flux periods. Using ∆B1 = 40.3 ± 6.7 mT and the 8% area term, the measured periods give ∆B1/∆B ≈ 6.8 ± 3.3 (−5/2), 3.1 ± 0.7 (−1/2) and 7.6 ± 2.4 (3/2). The −5/2 value is equally consistent with q = e/2 (p = 5). The −1/2 value lies about 1.7σ from p = 2. The ordering is inverted: the expectation is p(−5/2) > p(3/2), but ∆B−5/2 > ∆B3/2. So the magnetic data give at best weak independent support for e/4. The e/4 identification rests essentially on ∆V/∆V1 alone, and the phrase 'Within uncertainty, these periods correspond approximately to' hides this.
comments.suggested_fix: State p = |ν|e/q explicitly (citing Ref. [30] and Fig. S18). Report the measured ∆B1/∆B with propagated errors (≈6.8 ± 3.3, 3.1 ± 0.7, 7.6 ± 2.4) next to the predictions for q = e/4 (10, 2, 6) and q = e/2 (5, 1, 3), and say that the B data alone do not exclude e/2 at ν = −5/2.

comments.title: The nu = -1/2 doubled-regime B period is extracted from less than one period
comments.quote: For the double regime, a clear peak cannot be extracted and fitted for the magnetic field period in k,l, since there is no
comments.explanation: The authors are commendably open that no full period is present and that the half-period was estimated graphically. However, the main text builds a substantial argument on this number: p ≈ 1/3, an 'extremely large' period, an area reduction 'by close to a factor of ten', a possible intermediate regime and complex edge structure. Methods state dB = 1 mT and NB ≈ 101, so a scan spans about 100 mT, whereas p ≈ 1/3 implies ∆B ≈ 3∆B1 ≈ 120 mT, longer than the window. At that scale the FFT resolution (about 1/(100 mT)) puts the feature in the lowest bin, where the cubic background subtraction, slow drift and the magnet-supply instability mentioned in Methods all compete. A graphically estimated half-period of a feature longer than the scan cannot support a quantitative p value.
comments.suggested_fix: Report the ν = −1/2 doubled-regime period as a lower bound set by the scan window (∆B ≳ 100 mT, i.e. ∆B1/∆B ≲ 0.4) rather than as p ≈ 1/3, and drop the quantitative area-reduction argument that depends on it.

comments.title: The 'factor of ten' area reduction is overstated
comments.quote: which would require a reduction of the enclosed area by
comments.explanation: The factor of about ten seems to come from comparing the doubled-regime period (≈120 mT) with the minimal-regime period at ν = −1/2 (13 mT) while assuming the same p. But both scenarios the authors consider change p in the doubled regime. Bunching predicts p/2 = 1 at ν = −1/2, and the AB limit also predicts ∆B1/∆B = 1. In either case the expected doubled-regime period is about ∆B1 ≈ 40 mT with the reference area. The measured ∆B ≈ 3∆B1 then implies an area reduction by about 3, not 10. A factor of 3 is still large compared with the lB-scale edge displacements used elsewhere (8% per edge), so the qualitative point may survive, but the stated number overstates it.
comments.suggested_fix: Replace 'close to a factor of ten' with 'about a factor of three relative to the area implied by p = 1 (∆B ≈ 3∆B1)', and compare that with the expected side-gate-induced area change.

comments.title: The absence of doubling at odd-denominator states is not shown at comparable coupling
comments.quote: side-gate voltages of −2 V, and 0 V, respectively, while all other gate voltages are kept fixed.
comments.explanation: The state-selectivity of the doubling (present at −5/2, −1/2, 3/2, 2/3; absent at −4/3, −1/3) is used in the abstract framing, the Introduction and the Discussion to link the effect to edge structure and neutral modes. For ν = −1/3 the caption says a more positive side gate increases coupling, yet only −2 V and 0 V were measured. On the hole side, where ν = −1/2 doubled, the doubling appeared at 'increasingly positive' Vsg. So ν = −1/3 was never taken into the coupling-increasing direction. For ν = −4/3 the side gate reached 5 V, but the Vsg at which doubling sets in for −1/2 is not given, and coupling is never quantified (for example by the constriction filling factor or the backscattered fraction). A reader therefore cannot tell whether the odd-denominator states were driven to a coupling comparable to that at which the even-denominator states double. Supp. D also gives about 6 V as the safe limit while Fig. S6 gives 5 V.
comments.suggested_fix: For every state and side-gate setting in Figs. 3, S6 and S7, report a coupling measure (constriction filling factor from Rd, or δRt/Rt), and either show that ν = −1/3 and −4/3 reached at least the coupling at which ν = −1/2 and −5/2 double, or restrict the claim to 'no doubling up to the coupling reached'.

comments.title: Constriction filling factor in the doubled regime is not reported
comments.quote: As the absolute value of the constriction filling factor
comments.explanation: Earlier the authors state that the diagonal conductance is used to verify that the constriction filling remains close to the bulk value. Here the crossover is driven precisely by reducing the constriction filling. If, at the onset of doubling, the constriction has left the bulk plateau and sits on or near a neighbouring state (for example toward 4/3 or 1 at ν = 3/2, toward −1/3 or 0 at ν = −1/2, or toward 1/2 or 1/3 at ν = 2/3), then the AD-bound states are surrounded by a different fluid. The doubled period could then reflect that fluid rather than a new process of the bulk state. The ν = −1/2 discussion acknowledges something like this ('lower density fractional regions between the side gates and the AD'), but no Rd values are given for the doubled-regime data of any state.
comments.suggested_fix: Give the Rd-derived constriction filling factor for each dataset in Fig. 3d–o, and state whether it lies on the bulk plateau or on a different plateau when the doubled period is observed.

comments.title: Gate-period ratios cannot distinguish bunching from the nu_LL interferometry phenomenology
comments.quote: period ratios show a striking correspondence with recent
comments.explanation: The authors present the agreement of ∆V/∆V1 with νLL (1/2 for the even-denominator states, 2/3 at ν = 2/3) as a striking correspondence with AB interferometry. But for every state studied, the bunching scenario gives the same number: 2 × (1/4) = 1/2 and 2 × (1/3) = 2/3. So the 'correspondence' is just the observed factor-of-two doubling restated. It provides no evidence for the interferometry-like interpretation over bunching, and only the ∆B ratios can separate them. The next sentence ('The observed crossover therefore cannot be described as a complete transition to this limit') follows from the mismatch with ∆V/∆V1 = ν and ∆B1/∆B ≠ 1, not from the νLL correspondence, so the 'therefore' is misplaced.
comments.suggested_fix: Add: 'For all states studied here 2e*/e equals νLL, so the gate-period ratio alone cannot distinguish bunching from the νLL-controlled interference seen in BLG interferometers; the discrimination relies on the magnetic-field periods.' Move 'therefore' to the sentence comparing with ∆V/∆V1 = ν.

comments.title: Inconsistent suppression temperatures; the electron temperature is inferred, not measured
comments.quote: comparable energy scales, are suppressed in the same range of 30 mK to 50 mK, which places an upper bound on the
comments.explanation: The main text says the e/4 and doubled oscillations at −5/2 and 3/2 disappear at about 60 mK. Supp. L first says the e/4 oscillations are suppressed between 50 and 70 mK and the doubled ones above about 50 mK. This sentence then says all e/4 oscillations are suppressed between 30 and 50 mK. The temperature steps (16, 30, 50, 70 mK) cannot resolve these differences. In addition, the main text states an electron temperature 'of the order of 30–50 mK' as a fact and uses it, against 150 mK in Ref. [30], to explain why e/3 rather than 2e/3 dominates at ν = 2/3. By the authors' own account this number is only an upper bound from oscillation suppression, so the attribution rests on an inferred quantity.
comments.suggested_fix: Use one suppression range consistent with Fig. S16 throughout (e.g. 'between 50 and 70 mK'), and rephrase the main text as 'an electron temperature below about 50 mK, bounded by the suppression of the e/4 oscillations', or quote an independent thermometry value if one exists.

comments.title: Fitting statement contradicts Fig. S17d,e
comments.quote: including the minimal excitation oscillations of the even-denominator states, the amplitude is suppressed too rapidly
comments.explanation: This says the minimal-excitation oscillations of the even-denominator states are suppressed too quickly for a reliable amplitude extraction. Yet Fig. S17d,e and the last paragraph show and fit exactly such a dataset: the e/4 oscillations at ν = −1/2, 'described equally well by Eq. (1) and Eq. (4)'. A reader cannot tell which even-denominator minimal datasets were fitted.
comments.suggested_fix: Change to 'including the minimal excitation oscillations at ν = −5/2 and 3/2', since the ν = −1/2 e/4 oscillations are fitted in Fig. S17d,e.

comments.title: Temperature argument for a distinct mechanism at nu = -1/2 omits that nu = 2/3 behaves the same way
comments.quote: ν = −1/2, in contrast, the doubled-period oscillations
comments.explanation: The main text argues that the persistence of the ν = −1/2 doubled-period oscillations up to 120 mK sets it apart and suggests a different mechanism. Supp. L notes that the doubled oscillations at ν = 2/3 also persist to 120 mK. So the temperature data divide the doubled regimes into {−5/2, 3/2} and {−1/2, 2/3}, not '−1/2 versus the rest'. That bears directly on whether ν = −1/2 is anomalous. Separately, a common suppression temperature for the e/4 and doubled oscillations at −5/2 and 3/2 is called consistent with 'the same underlying e/4 quasiparticles'. Any two processes governed by the same AD charging or level-spacing scale would show that, so it is weak evidence.
comments.suggested_fix: Add to the main text: 'The doubled-period oscillations at ν = 2/3 likewise persist up to 120 mK (Supp. Material)', and change 'consistent with ... originating from the same underlying e/4 quasiparticles' to 'consistent with, but not proof of, a common energy scale'.

comments.title: The capacitive model does not confirm area rather than density oscillations
comments.quote: agreement confirms that the ADG oscillations are area oscillations rather than density oscillations.
comments.explanation: The series-capacitance formula itself is correct, but it describes the air gap and the top hBN in series under the bridge, not 'the ADG and the top graphite gate' in series. The problems are in the comparison. (i) It uses dtg = 50 nm, whereas Methods give 46 nm (which gives a factor of about 11.4, not 10). (ii) The bridge height 'can vary significantly', so the factor is unconstrained. The measured ratio 235/33 ≈ 7.1 implies dbridge ≈ 95 nm, well below the expected 160 nm. (iii) The predicted 330 mV differs from the measured 235 mV by 40%, which is described as 'closer to' and 'agreement'. (iv) The TG+BG area period at ν = −2 (field not stated) is compared with the ADG period at ν = −1 and 10 T. (v) Most importantly, a geometric capacitance ratio scales any electrostatically driven period, area-type or density-type alike, so matching it cannot discriminate between the two mechanisms. This matters because the paper uses the area character of ADG oscillations to rule out the slope method.
comments.suggested_fix: Describe the model as air gap and hBN in series, use dtg = 46 nm, state that the measured ratio ∆Vadg/∆Vtg ≈ 7 corresponds to dbridge ≈ 95 nm, and replace 'This agreement confirms ... rather than density oscillations' with 'This is consistent with the ADG acting through a weaker, purely geometric capacitance'. Rest the area-versus-density distinction on the TG-versus-ADG comparison of Supp. G instead.

comments.title: Area correction is applied uniformly and only to the B ratio, not to the gate ratio
comments.quote: interest. We estimate this change by assuming that each
comments.explanation: The estimate (one lB per additional edge state, giving 2lB/R ≈ 8% for R = 180 nm at 14 T) is reasonable as an order of magnitude, and the arithmetic checks out. But a single 8% term is applied to all states, although the number of additional edges relative to ν = −1 differs between states (for example, ν = −5/2 has more than one extra edge). The reference is taken at 10 T (lB ≈ 8.1 nm) while the data are at 14 T, and the area difference between fields is not included. Most importantly, the same change in AD-bound-state radius also changes the ADG-to-AD coupling, and therefore ∆V/∆V1, which is the main evidence for e/4. No corresponding term is propagated into the gate ratios. The ν = −4/3 benchmark reads 0.37 rather than 0.333, an 11% offset of the same size as these effects. The sentence 'when taking ratios of gate voltage periods to determine ∆B1/∆B' also mixes up the two quantities.
comments.suggested_fix: Scale the area term with the number of additional edges, n × 2lB/R (about 16% for two extra edges), include the 10 T versus 14 T difference in lB, and propagate an equivalent lever-arm uncertainty into ∆V/∆V1. Change 'ratios of gate voltage periods' to 'ratios of magnetic-field periods'.

comments.title: Electron-side states are normalized to a hole-side reference
comments.quote: with relatively small error. We therefore use ν = −1 at 10 T as the integer reference.
comments.explanation: From the side-gate polarities (positive Vsg increases coupling on the hole side, Fig. S1e and Fig. 3) and the silicon-gate settings, negative ν is the hole side. All calibration points in Fig. S3 (ν = −1 at 10 and 14 T, ν = −2, ν = −4/3) are on the hole side. Yet ∆V1 and ∆B1 from ν = −1 are used to normalize ν = 2/3 and 3/2, which are on the electron side and use opposite silicon-gate and side-gate polarity, and possibly a different BG setting for the AD potential. BLG has electron-hole asymmetry, and the ADG lever arm and effective AD area need not be equal for the two carrier types. The fact that 3/2 gives 0.25 and 2/3 gives 0.32 is reassuring but circular, because these are the values being tested. The terminology adds confusion: Fig. 4 calls ν = −1, −4/3 and −1/3 'electron-like' while they are on the hole side.
comments.suggested_fix: Add an electron-side benchmark, either ν = +1 (or +2) to obtain an electron-side ∆V1 and ∆B1, or an electron-side odd-denominator state such as ν = 1/3 or 4/3 normalized to the ν = −1 reference. Rename 'electron-like' in Fig. 4 to 'particle-like'.

comments.title: Figure panel references swapped between nu = -1/2 and 2/3
comments.quote: As shown in Fig. 3d,e for ν = 2/3, and similarly
comments.explanation: According to the Fig. 3 caption and the earlier text, panels d–f show ν = −1/2 and panels g–i show ν = 2/3. This sentence assigns d,e to ν = 2/3 and g,i to ν = −1/2. Because the point being made (doubling over the same ADG range when only Vsg changes) is checked by looking at specific panels, the swap could send a reader to the wrong data.
comments.suggested_fix: Change to 'As shown in Fig. 3g,i for ν = 2/3, and similarly for ν = −1/2 in Fig. 3d,f'.

comments.title: Factor of two in the thermal dephasing scale relative to the standard result
comments.quote: so that ∆E = 4π 2 kB T0 .
comments.explanation: Eqs. (2) and (3) are internally consistent: with ∆E = 2ℏv/D = hv/(2πR) and kBT0 = ℏv/(4π²R), the ratio is indeed 4π². However, the standard thermal smearing of an interference term with level spacing ∆E (the Lifshitz-Kosevich-type factor x/sinh x, x = 2π²kBT/∆E) gives an exponential decay exp(−2π²kBT/∆E) at high T, i.e. kBT0 = ∆E/(2π²) = ℏv/(2π²R), a factor of two larger than Eq. (2). Conventions differ between references, and the T0 value is used only qualitatively ('T ≈ 2T0'), so the impact is small. But the relation between T0 and ∆E should be stated with its source and convention.
comments.suggested_fix: Either use kBT0 = ℏv/(2π²R), so that ∆E = 2π²kBT0, consistent with the x/sinh x thermal factor, or state which convention of Ref. [59] gives the extra factor of two.

comments.title: Comparing R² across differently linearised fits is not a valid model comparison
comments.quote: The two models are compared through the coefficient of determination R2 of their respective linearised regressions.
comments.explanation: The exponential model is linearised as ln A vs T and the power law as ln A vs ln T. R² values computed on different transformed abscissae are not comparable measures of goodness of fit to the same data. In addition, a T^−1 peak-height law is the quantum Coulomb-blockade result (single level resolved, ∆E ≫ kBT). The Conclusion implies this regime is not reached in the present antidot ('In smaller antidots, where the single-level splitting exceeds the temperature scale...'). The authors' own conclusion that the fits are indistinguishable limits the damage, but the procedure as stated cannot support a preference for either model.
comments.suggested_fix: Fit both models directly to A(T) on the same scale and compare reduced χ² (or AIC) computed on A itself, and note that α ≈ 1 is expected only for ∆E ≫ kBT.

comments.title: Attribution of the nu = 2/3 instability is asserted without support, and the source of the quoted gate ratio is unclear
comments.quote: In our case the instability cannot be related to
comments.explanation: The authors exclude quasiparticles entering and leaving the AD-bulk without giving a reason, and instead attribute the hysteresis to two nearly degenerate configurations that localize e/3 or 2e/3. If that is right, the minimal-regime ν = 2/3 data mix e/3 and 2e/3 behaviour (Fig. S14b sometimes needs two Gaussians), which weakens the clean e/3 claim. Meanwhile the main text quotes ∆V/∆V1 = 0.32 ± 0.03 without saying whether it comes from the 2D-FFT, which Supp. K says 'cannot directly be considered reliable', or from the histogram centres, which are shown but not tabulated.
comments.suggested_fix: State which method gives ∆V/∆V1 = 0.32 ± 0.03 at ν = 2/3, report the fitted e/3 and 2e/3 histogram centres and their relative weights from Fig. S14b, and either justify excluding bulk quasiparticle switching (for example by its B dependence) or present it as an alternative.

comments.title: Overreach about why earlier experiments did not resolve e/4
comments.quote: cates that the absence of resolved charge-e/4 and e/3 pe-
comments.explanation: The Introduction itself notes that the BLG interferometry experiments [22–24] did find localized e/4 excitations enclosed by the interferometer, while the interfering charge was e/2. Interferometers measure the interfering (braiding-phase) charge, which is a different quantity from the CD charge-addition period measured here. Showing that a weakly coupled antidot resolves e/4 does not establish that the e/2 interference periodicity in [22–24] is extrinsic, so 'unlikely to be intrinsic to the states themselves' overreaches for those references. It is better supported for the antidot results at ν = 2/3 [28, 30].
comments.suggested_fix: Restrict the sentence to antidot measurements: '...the absence of resolved e/3 periodicity in earlier antidot measurements of ν = 2/3 [28, 30] is unlikely to be intrinsic', and add that interferometry probes the interfering charge, which need not equal the localized charge.

comments.title: Meaning of the quoted period uncertainties is ambiguous
comments.quote: The error obtained in this way accounts for both the
comments.explanation: Methods describe Gaussian fits to the 2D-FFT line cuts and to histograms, and the S4–S6 captions say the Gaussian widths 'characterize the spread' of the peaks. It is not stated whether the quoted errors (e.g. ±0.03 on ∆V/∆V1) are fit uncertainties on the Gaussian centre or the Gaussian width σ. These differ greatly, especially for FFT peaks whose width is set by the finite scan window. The ν = −5/2 case, where a fit error of 2.8 mV was doubled to 5.6 mV 'in line with the other states', suggests that centre errors are used, with ad hoc adjustment. Since the e/4 versus e/3 distinction at ν = −5/2 (0.27 ± 0.03 against 0.333) depends on the error size, this should be explicit.
comments.suggested_fix: State that the quoted uncertainty is the standard error of the fitted Gaussian centre (or σ, if so), give the Vadg scan range and FFT resolution δfV for each dataset, and list in one table where the histogram error replaced the FFT error.

comments.title: AB-limit gate-period argument mixes the side gate and the ADG
comments.quote: flects the localized quasiparticle charge. For an ideal side
comments.explanation: The prediction ∆V/∆V1 = ν in the AB limit is stated for 'an ideal side gate that primarily changes the enclosed area', followed by an assumption about the 'ADG-to-area lever arm'. In this experiment the side gates tune the coupling and the ADG is the swept gate whose period is measured. The sentence reads as if the side gate were the swept gate, which may lead a reader to apply the model to the wrong gate.
comments.suggested_fix: Replace 'For an ideal side gate' with 'For an ideal antidot gate (here the ADG)'.
